title: On Missing Labels, Long-tails and Propensities in Extreme Multi-label Classification

problem.claim: Extreme multi-label classification must address missing and long-tail labels.

gap.claim: The application of the standard propensity-based approach in contemporary XMLC works is debatable despite its theoretical soundness.

contributions.claim: The paper discusses flaws in the propensity-based approach for XMLC.
The paper presents several alternative recipes for addressing missing and long-tail labels in XMLC.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report an exhaustive discussion of flaws in the propensity-based approach.
The authors characterize the proposed alternative recipes as promising.

narrative_sequence.summary: Propensity modeling is described as a standard approach for missing and long-tail labels in XMLC.
The paper challenges the practical application of that approach in contemporary XMLC work.
The paper discusses flaws and proposes several alternative recipes, including ideas related to search engines and recommender systems.

source_observation.claim: A theoretically sound approach may still have debatable applicability in contemporary systems.

interpretation.claim: Method selection should evaluate practical deployment assumptions in addition to theoretical justification.

application.claim: When adapting a standard XMLC method, assess whether its assumptions fit current data and system conditions.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify the conditions under which the propensity approach remains appropriate.

unknowns: The abstract does not identify the specific flaws in the propensity-based approach.
The abstract does not describe the alternative recipes in detail.
The abstract does not report datasets, metrics, numerical results, or independent validation.
